newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta weakens but not seen breaking 84.45/mark.
newsitem.headline: Peseta weakens but not seen breaking 84.45/mark.

text.p: Despite an opening slide amid fresh worries on European economic and monetary union (EMU), the peseta is seen trading relatively stable on Friday with the mark seen staying below key resistance at around 84.45, dealers said.
"The peseta was too strong before the official rate cut," a dealer in Madrid said.
"Today, it softened just a bit amid this apparently new round of EMU jitters".
At 0810 GMT the peseta was trading at 84.41/43 per mark after having closed on Thursday at 84.31/33.
It was trading at around 84.12 on Tuesday when the Bank of Spain announced its third rate cut in the year by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.
On Friday the peseta weakened amid fresh worries about prospects for the start of the European single currency.

Rumours of a possible snap election in France are adding pessimism as dealers said a possible change in power there will be considered as a likely halt to a timely start of the Europe's single currency.
Also unconfirnmed newspaper reports of a European Commission forecast which says Italy will not meet EMU targets were pulling down Italian assets and adding pressure to the peseta.
Dealers in Madrid added that the market turned more pessimistic yesterday afternoon as Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he was opposed to a softening of the strict EMU criteria.
